comments.content: Changing the default `thinking_budget` from `None` to `0` is a behavior change: previously no `thinking_config` was sent (letting the model use its default), now `thinking_config={'thinking_budget': -1}` is always sent. Combined with the change below that hardcodes `-1` (dynamic thinking) regardless of the user-provided value, this makes the `thinking_budget` field effectively ignored. If the intent is to default to dynamic thinking, consider keeping `None` as the default and only sending `thinking_config` when explicitly set, or at least document the new default.

The user-supplied `self.thinking_budget` value is discarded here — `thinking_budget` is hardcoded to `-1` (dynamic). This means callers can no longer disable thinking (e.g. `thinking_budget=0`) or set a fixed budget. If the goal is to force dynamic thinking, remove the field; otherwise use `self.thinking_budget` here.

The manual retry loop with `_is_retryable_error` was removed and replaced with a comment claiming the Google client handles retries internally. The default `google-genai` client does not retry on 429/5xx by default unless `HttpOptions` with retry settings is configured. This is a regression in resilience for rate-limited or transient failures. Either configure retries on the client (e.g. via `HttpOptions`/`retry` in `_get_client_params`) or keep the manual retry loop.

`asyncio.CancelledError` is a `BaseException` in Python 3.8+, not an `Exception`, so it will not be caught by `except Exception as e` here. The `isinstance(e, asyncio.CancelledError)` branch is therefore dead code. If you want to handle cancellation, catch `asyncio.CancelledError` explicitly (and be aware that swallowing it can break task cancellation semantics).
